# Current state — legeos

What the project believes right now: live terms, constraints, policies and requirements, and what has been found or assessed. Decisions have their own view, `DECISION-HISTORY.md`.

## Terms

## Constraints

### The first release does not attempt a custom kernel, libc, package format/manager, display protocol, object filesystem, universal checkpointing, all NVIDIA generations, an app store, phone/tablet/server editions, or third-party shell extensions

`active` · `@legeos.constraint.first-release-scope/1` · scope `all` · topic `first-release-scope`

Until the five first-release claims are proven, LegeOS keeps systemd, cgroup v2, APT/Debian packages, standard filesystems, PipeWire, NetworkManager, BlueZ, Mesa and the upstream NVIDIA userspace stack. It does not build: a Linux kernel fork, a new package format or manager, a new libc/basic userland, replacement networking/Bluetooth/audio stacks, a new display protocol, a semantic/object filesystem replacing paths, transparent checkpointing of arbitrary applications, support for every old NVIDIA generation, a complete alternative application store, phone/tablet/server editions, or extensions/third-party shell plugins.

### Identity comes from the launch cgroup, never from a client's self-declared app_id; Exec= is never run through a shell; the governor is observe-only until traces are reviewed and never selects a victim by memory size alone

`active` · `@legeos.constraint.identity-and-launch-safety/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-appd/**"`, `path "crates/lege-window/**"`, `path "services/lege-resourced/**"` · topic `identity-launch-governor-safety`

(1) A window's application identity is resolved PID -> cgroup -> instance -> canonical AppId; client claims (Wayland app_id, WM_CLASS, sandbox id) can only lower confidence (claim mismatch) or, when unique, yield claim-only confidence — never override a verified launch, and privileged actions require verified-launch. (2) Applications are launched as the registered executable plus an argument vector in a dedicated systemd unit; Exec= lines are parsed, never passed to a shell. (3) lege-resourced ships observe-only; enforcement (memory.high, reclaim, checkpoint, cgroup.kill) is enabled in stages after recorded traces are reviewed; the victim score weighs growth, PSI contribution, foreground/visible state, unsaved work and disposability, never resident size alone; session-critical units are never candidates.

### Exactly one selected provider per exclusive system role may autostart

`active` · `@legeos.constraint.one-provider-per-role/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-session-core/src/autostart.rs"`, `path "crates/lege-session-core/src/providers.rs"`, `path "crates/lege-types/src/provider.rs"` · topic `one-provider-per-role`

For every ProviderRole (network-status-ui, notification-server, file-chooser, file-manager, lock-screen, association-broker, clipboard-manager, power-manager, screenshot-service, input-method, portal-backend, greeter) installing a second provider never silently starts both; the user or distribution policy selects one and only that one autostarts.

### Every component is a Debian package (nothing under /usr/local or untracked in $HOME); lege-window carries no async runtime or D-Bus dependency

`active` · `@legeos.constraint.packaging-and-render-thread/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-window/**"`, `path "debian/**"`, `path "tools/xtask/**"` · topic `packaging-and-render-thread`

All binaries, units, manifests and policy files are installed by Debian packages (cargo-deb now, the vendored source package later); development installs go through a local apt repository. The compositor-side lege-window crate must never depend on tokio, zbus, async-std or smol because it runs on the compositor render thread.

### System behaviour belongs in services; tray icons, panels and applets are views

`active` · `@legeos.constraint.services-not-indicators/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-session-core/**"`, `path "services/**"`, `path "shell/**"` · topic `services-not-indicators`

No policy (timezone discovery, power decisions, autostart choices, association defaults, notification storage) is implemented in a shell surface or applet; each lives in a service crate/daemon with a D-Bus interface, and the shell only renders and forwards user choices.

### M1: the governor defaults to observe-only and performs nothing above its stage

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-governor-staged/1`

Stage defaults to observe-only; an action above the current stage is decided, scored, signalled with applied=false and not performed. RestoreDynamicLimits only writes when the governor itself placed the override, so observe-only performs no cgroup write at all with an application present — tested directly. Traces record pressure episodes and level changes rather than idle ticks, so the ring holds episodes rather than wall-clock noise. 62 tests.

### M1: a journalled file operation resumes without redoing completed work

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-operations-resume/1`

A move interrupted after its copy step resumes from the journalled cursor and does not copy again — proved by rewriting the source with different bytes of the same length between the interruption and the resume and asserting the destination still holds the original. Every step is applied twice in a test to prove idempotence, and a conflicting destination fails before the source is touched. 66 tests in lege-filed.

### M1: session policy survives a restart and instances are re-derived

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-session-persists/1`

Associations, provider selections and declarations, autostart approvals, settings values and their change log, projects and history all load from the one SQLite store at start and write through it, with a cross-domain change committing as one transaction; live instances are re-derived from systemd unit names on restart. Smoke-run against this machine's 208 real desktop entries, twice, idempotently. 90 tests across the session track.

### M1: the update transaction resumes in every phase and cannot brick the machine

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-update-transaction-resumes/1`

Seeding the journal at each phase shows the right apt and snapshot calls re-run and the wrong ones do not, including mid-phase: Staging resumes with a partially populated candidate directory and Verifying with boot files already written, both reaching AwaitingReboot. Both boot backends work against a command-runner fake. lege-boot-health may only force a reboot on a boot genuinely trialling a candidate, so an ordinary boot cannot loop. 89 tests, none needing NVIDIA, btrfs, an ESP or apt.

### M1: windows stay recoverable across drag, hotplug, scale change and restore

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-windows-recoverable/1`

Eight 2000-case property tests over generated multi-output topologies (mixed scales, negative origins, overlapping and disjoint arrangements) prove repair implies recoverable, repair is idempotent and size-preserving, the show-all-windows scatter stays inside the active outputs, and the drag anchor is scale-independent; a further 300-case test covers hotplug sequences and deterministic migration. 69 tests across lege-window and lege-comp-integration.
